text: #359's in-place proof in the gate, for @gitdek's ratification, in place of D-0258 and D-0259 after #359's third review, by one principle: what ordinary code does is never called proved when it isn't, so the gate refuses it; deliberate tampering at run time is refused where that's cheap, and the rest is named below as assumed. verify.Check and verify.Run admit a check that selects an in-place proof of a Python function only beside conformance on the same function; the direct Python check refuses it, since it returns no proof. verify.Check refuses, before any tool runs, what the function's own source shows the gate can't prove: what the verifier input can't preserve of the function, an async function, a decorator, Pure included, since conformance binds only undecorated functions, Assume, which has Nagini take a fact nothing proves, a contract that couldn't run as Nagini reads it, and arithmetic the pinned Nagini models apart from Python. The module runs with Invariant's runtime stand-in for nagini_contracts, so Python calls each contract statement where it stands and evaluates its arguments then, a postcondition on entry and an Implies' consequent whether or not its antecedent holds. So Nagini's names may appear only in contract statements, Requires, Ensures, Exsures, Decreases, Assert and Invariant, whose calls must bind as the stand-in takes them, and their arguments may hold only names, literals and tuples of them, Result(), Old() and the stand-in's other names, comparisons, and, or and not, conditional expressions, +, - and *, // and % by a positive integer literal, written as a plain int constant and not a bool, unary + and -, and calls of len, abs and isinstance, the last with int, bool, str, bytes, list, tuple, dict, set or object. They may order, do arithmetic on, and take the len or abs of only what the gate can tell has one builtin type that operation can't fail on: by a parameter's annotation, a literal, a display, the builtin that makes it, a module's literal constant, or for a local every binding of it. They may read an Optional or a Union only in is, is not and isinstance tests, test membership only in what the gate can tell is a builtin container that can hold what's tested, Result() only in a tuple the contract lists, repeat a sequence only by an int literal, and read a local only where every path to it binds the local first. Result() returns an inert value that answers every allowed operator, reflected forms included, made afresh, class and all, on every call. The arithmetic rule holds for the function's body and contract alike, and for every trusted contract's abstraction the proof assumes: // and % only by a positive integer literal, since the pinned Nagini divides as Viper's Euclidean division does, which isn't Python's for a negative divisor; none of the bitwise operators, and, or, exclusive or and invert, which it models apart from Python on negative ints; no / and no float at all, a float or complex literal, float(), a float annotation, constant or abstraction signature among them, since it leaves floats uninterpreted while Python fails converting an int too large for one; and multiplication only of what the gate can tell are both ints, or by an int literal, since repeating a sequence past what CPython can index fails where Nagini's model doesn't. Shifts and ** stay, since Nagini's preconditions on them are where Python raises. Once the session has staged the application and selected its dependency image, before any test, conformance, backing test or Nagini runs, the gate refuses what depends on the rest of the application: a binding, a trusted contract or a production source the verifier input can't stand for, and a nagini_contracts that isn't Invariant's stand-in. The application must ship the stand-in at its root, exactly its __init__.py and contracts.py and nothing else in that package, and no other nagini_contracts anywhere else in it; a selected function may read only the names the stand-in's __all__, a tuple, exports. The scan for writes protects nagini_contracts, its contracts module and the builtins as it does the function's module, across the application's production sources: writing their attributes, reaching them through sys.modules, by name or through a patcher, reading their __dict__ or another special attribute, handing them to a call, vars and reload included, and reading the namespace of a source that holds one are refused. Where production code runs beside the module, in it, the packages on its way, every production source that loads one of them, directly or through others, and all those load, the scan also refuses running or compiling code from a path, a string or a code object, exec, eval and compile under any name a scope around them doesn't bind; reaching modules through inspect.getmodule or gc; reading __globals__, f_globals, f_builtins, __builtins__ or a builtin function's __self__, which is the builtins module, or taking one by name where a getattr-style call or a namespace's lookup takes it; writing a function's __code__, __defaults__ or __kwdefaults__ other than to a literal; using sys.meta_path, sys.path_hooks or sys.path_importer_cache, which can load another module in place of one the proof takes as it ships; using sys.modules other than to look a module up by a constant name; and importing or patching by a name the source computes. A compiled module, .pyc, .so or .pyd, that production code loads, or that stands where the module or a package on its way would be, is refused, since the scan can't read it. After the application's tests, conformance and backing tests, the gate runs the pinned Nagini from its recipe on each input, apart from the application's image, records each attempt in the application report and attributes its result as component proof evidence. A proof qualifies only as an effective guarantee: the function proved from its original bytes, with no error and nothing it reached unaccounted for, every trusted contract it assumed tested, and conformance on the same function passing in the same session against the same source bytes, since the collector binds what conformance observes to that very staged declaration. A proof that doesn't qualify fails the gate. One Nagini verified is marked unqualified in the report, which later attribution keeps, and receipts call it not qualified and leave it out of the proved count. A receipt counts an in-place result, which its in_place_input pin marks, only beside the attempt that pin names, and shows each proof as holding only on the condition that its trusted contracts hold. Fingerprints bind each attempt's input, recipe and result, never its local image, its command, Nagini's output or its timing. A proof covers only the selected function's own body: no dependency, no unselected function and not the whole application. What stays assumed: calls whose function is computed, and other reflection the parse can't follow; what the application's dependencies and startup run; ctypes and other ways around Python's own semantics; that arguments are values of the builtin types their annotations name, not instances of subclasses with operators of their own or of other types, since checking callers is #210's; that no change to the import path loads a nagini_contracts a dependency installs in place of the stand-in; that what runs beside the module reaches it through imports and constant names the scan follows, not through configuration a framework reads; Nagini's own model of the builtins it models, their exceptions included; and the trusted contracts themselves, which their backing tests support and nothing proves.
